newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Cargo partly blamed for KLM Q2 results.
newsitem.headline: Cargo partly blamed for KLM Q2 results.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines partly blamed a weak cargo market for its disappointing second quarter results.

Cargo capacity growth had been reduced and was now within range of traffic growth, KLM stated. Cargo load factor again decreased, this time by 0.4 percent to 66 percent in the second quarter. But this compared to a 3.3 percent point decrease in the first quarter.

In the second quarter, KLM capacity to and from North America had been reduced by six percent which was mainly in the cargo market and by shifting services to Northwest Airlines, the airline stated. Increased capacity and traffic in the Middle East/South Asia markets were mainly the result of the introduction of a Boeing 767.
The cargo load factor on intercontinental routes increased slightly in the second quarter compared to the previous year's second quarter. Cargo traffic revenues were three percent higher.

But yield per revenue ton-kilometre (RTK) in guilders declined three percent to NLG cents 42.2 per RTK; "as a result of negative changes in product mix, in average distance flown and positive exchange rate differences of approximately two percent." Unit revenue in NLG cents per availableTK (ATK)) fell by four percent to NLG cents 27.9 for the second quarter.
